Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 



( Reaffirmed 2006 ) 



SPECIFICATION FOR 
KNIFE, DOWNWARD CUTTING, ZOELLNER'S PATTERN 



1. Scope — Covers dimensional and ottier requirements for downward cutting Zoellner's knife used 
in ENT microsurgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1. 





DETAIL AT 2 




ENLARGED 
SECTION XX 

All dimensions In millimetres. 
FIG. 1 KNIFE. DOWNWARD CUTTING, ZOELLNER'S PATTERN 

2.1 A deviation of ± 2"5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions. 

3. Material — Stainless steel conforming to the Designation 30Cr13 of 18:6603-1972 'Specification 
for stainless steel bars and flats '. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 All edges other than the cutting edge of the knife shall be rounded. 

4.2 The cutting edge shall be surgically sharp. 

4.3 The knife shall be free from feathers, kincks, high spots, waviness or undulation when examined 
under a magnification of 60x. 

4.4 The cutting edge of the knife shall be centred and in one plane passing through the centre of the 
handle, 

4.5 The knife shall be passivated and matt finished. 

4.6 Proper grooves shall be provided in the handle for easy grip^

INDIAN STANDARDS INSTITUTION

18:9059-1979 

4.7 The knife shall be forged in one piece to the required shape and size. 

4.8 The knife shall be well balanced. 

5. Heat Treatment — The knife shall be hardened and tempered to a hardness of 380 to 480 HV. 

6. Tests 

6-1 Flexibility — The knife shall be held from the handle in a vice with the blade projecting above the 
jaws. A force shall be applied at 8*5 mm from tip of the blade so as to displace it through 5 mm in 
a plane perpendicular to the plane passing through the axis and the cutting edge of the blade. On 
releasing the force the blade shall return to its normal position without being damaged or taking 
any permanent set. 

6.2 Sharpness of the Cutting Edge — The knife shall be made to cut a piece of chamois leather. Five 
such cuts 25 mm long approximately shall be made. The knife shall cut the chamois leather cleanly 
and without pulling the leather. 

6.3 Corrosion Resistance — The knife shall show no sign of corrosion when tested in accordance 
with IS: 7531"1975 'Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless 
steel surgical instruments'. 

7. Marking — The knife shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or registered trade- 
mark. 

7.1 ISI Certification MarA/ng — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — The knife shall be thoroughly cleaned, preferably ultrasonically, and dried before 
packing. The knife shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper or packed in polyethylene bag. Each 
knife shall then be packed in individual carton in such a way that its working end is protected from 
coming in contact with hard surface resulting in any damage. The knife may also be packed as 
agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
